item.title: Re: LOOKING FOR GREENLIGHT/SCP Early concept: the greatest artist
item.content:encoded:
A little verbose on the history front, but I think we're getting somewhere.

+ show block
– hide block

humans always found a need to do art, of course there were different kinds of art but it was always art, so it tried to copy us thourhgt the years and believed that replicating our art is the way to comprehend what is "being human" so it currently is in this endless loop it tries to make art

This is probably as close to motivation as we can get; a desire to be human by means of expressing what it believes to be human expressions. The additional "loss of identity" aspect is a bit so-so, but it's workable. This is good!

I think the narrative of the article could revolve around the scientist breaking it's current delusional state of existence where he is so deep in the whole "Mimicing humans" thing it thinks each one of its forms are actual people with actual life historys, and after that facade is broken they could get him psychological assistance.

I really like this idea! It doesn't necessarily need to be something that the doctor means to do. Maybe they just get fed up with the mistaken identity act and they verbally lash out. You could play with that a little, too; the entity could use the doctor's outrage as it's own inspiration and couple it with realization of what it truly is.

i plan to write this all way more subtly than here ofc but that's what I have so far

Subtlety is important, yes, but you should also make sure that you don't sacrifice your core story elements by underplaying them. This is fiction. It is equally important to play up moments to engage the reader.

I'm glad to see that you've taken the time to rethink your approach to this idea. I'm not sure how much more I can do on the brainstorming side here, so it might be better to see how you've decided to execute it. Consider this a greenlight. You do need to two to use the Drafts Forums, so if that is something you'd like to pursue, I suggest reaching out to another reviewer, perhaps by utilizing our Butterfly Squad Roster.

Good luck.

item.title: Re: LOOKING FOR GREENLIGHT/SCP Early concept: the greatest artist
item.content:encoded:
Responding to PM request (even though I'm listed as not taking requests for the time being, but hey, 'tis the season, right?)

So, I'm admittedly not super impressed here. I think there's a decent base to work with in regards to what the anomaly is capable of, which is shape-shifting into this very specific thing of art style mimicry. Giving it a personality centered around fascination of how humans express themselves through art is a good trait and can be tied into a narrative very neatly, I think.

There are, however, some snags that are keeping me from really enjoying this. There's this underlying murderous intent that doesn't make any sense to me. There's this drive to "be good at art" that feels contrived. And these are two big aspects of the character, making them kind of glaringly not appealing.

Which is what I want to focus on a bit. I think the character of the anomaly here needs a bit of shaping up and applied to a narrative that makes sense for it. If the anomaly's fascinations revolve around the history of human art, then what do its goals become? Are its efforts of artistic expression rooted in a desire to be human? Does it have a unique inner conflict that it can only express through mastery of an artistic medium that it has yet to find? People are often defined by their motivations and desires, which are often shaped by their past. What is this character trying to do, how does it get there, and what (if anything) gets in its way?

Feel free to reach out to me on IRC and we can talk this out a little more. I'm usually in all the chats, but it'd be better to hit me up in #thecritters.

item.title: Re: SCP Early concept: the greatest artist
item.content:encoded: I really like the idea here, I think it's pretty unique, but I'm a little confused with how the immortality and multiple identities work. You say the scp is impossible to kill, but can die. Does this mean that it is impervious to any weapons, but can die from old age or disease? and in that case, does it just live a normal human life span until dying and being reincarnated as one of the 10 different forms? If that is how it works, I think a cool idea to add would be that within each of its life spans, it, as you describe, goes from asking for basic supplies, to more extreme mediums, and at the end of each life span it attempts to do something SUPER dangerous and the foundation has to do something to stop it each time. I'm not sure how dangerous art could be lol, but maybe you could think of something.

All of the instances are kind of the same entity and not the same entity at the same time.
They all have certain memories which are shared between all instances, but none of the instances know about each other and their experiences, the scientist's current hypothesis is that it is an entity who got way too much into character for these caricatures of people, kind of dissociating and losing its sense of self, the only evidence is that they all have certain key memories that are shared between them all, so, for now, it's quite the stretch.

item.title: SCP Early concept: the greatest artist
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:This SCP is an unidentified being that has shown itself quite fascinated by human art, it regularly shape-shifts between 6 forms, each representing an art movement in history, these forms vary from a stoic Egyptian Pharaoh to a very surreal blob of energy that is a visual representation of the concept of "Abstract" the thing all of these instances share in common is the desire to produce a masterpiece, any damage to their art can and will be retaliated.

This SCP requests increasingly more and higher quality art supplies to make its own art, it went from being satisfied with paper and crayons to demanding the amount of paint equivalent of what would be needed to paint the Sistine Chapple.

This SCP wants to create art, if its art supplies are not provided quickly it will find a suitable replacement, by any means necessary, for example shaping a human bone enough to make it able to carve a hieroglyph on a wall.

See more
See Less

Central Narrative: after the SCP is secured when it was shapeshifting and crying all the while obsessively staring at a painting in a museum, a particular incident will happen where the SCP freaked out about just not understanding humans and breaking its character of being a human that put him on the radar of this particular scientist who proceeded to have multiple conversations with the SCP, some indulging it in its delusions of being human and sometimes just being very brutal and pointing out how he's just some poor caricature of humanity without any nuance, eventually the SCP will have a meltdown that will ultimately result into it breaking out of its delusions and slowly remembering it's origins as a being that has been observing our species through the sidelines, and tried to mimic us, using art as a landmark since it was the only consistent thing we did throught our whole history.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think that an SCP whose abilities are directly connected with art history is quite a fascinating idea, and something that I least think has not been done in this way.

Additional Notes: Here are some random concepts based on several critiques I've had

  • Maybe they are very insecure about their art and request feedback and while they say there are open to constructive criticism they really aren't and will try to kill anyone who gives negative feedback
